name: harness-stale-read-names-the-writing-session
description: R15, DISTINGUISH HALF. Session A reads, peer session B acquires and commits, A re-reads and is told it is stale -- and `summary.last_writer_session_id` names B. That field is the whole point: a client decides whether to re-read based on WHO moved the bytes underneath it, and the A-pin and the B-pin below differ for a real reason. Read the `preserve_identity` declaration as intent, NOT as the thing making this assertion work: the field names the writing AGENT, whose id is 32-char hex, and the portability scrub is 8-4-4-4-12 only -- so the default never touched this value and this fixture compares identically with the declaration deleted. That is not a hole (both runtimes derive the id the same way from the session id the fixture itself supplies, so it is deterministic rather than backend noise) but it does mean this fixture cannot OBSERVE the opt-in; `test_the_writer_field_is_portable_by_derivation_not_by_scrubbing` says so directly, and fixture 03 -- `sessions[].agent_id` on /status, which IS hyphenated and IS collapsed by the default -- is where the mechanism is exercised. The declaration stays because it states the contract for the field and would be correct again the moment the spelling is. The two timestamps and the prose context stay ignored (they vary per run, following warn_mode/14); the ATTRIBUTION is the contract.
